summary_paragraph: The patient with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass presented with one day of epigastric pain with nausea and a single non-bloody, non-bilious emesis and increased loose stools. Evaluation included labs without leukocytosis, CT abdomen/pelvis showing oral contrast in both the gastric pouch and remnant suggesting possible fistulous communication and mild proximal efferent limb dilation without obstruction, and EGD demonstrating a widely patent gastrojejunostomy with two perianastomotic jejunal ulcers (one superficial clean-based and one deeper cratered ulcer) without active bleeding; H. pylori serology was negative. She was treated with IV morphine transitioned to oral oxycodone-acetaminophen solution, started on IV Protonix then transitioned to oral PPI, and her diet was advanced from Bariatric Stage 2 to Stage III with a lactose-free modification for diarrhea. With improved pain control and tolerance of oral intake/medications, she was discharged home on crushed omeprazole BID with return precautions and follow-up planning.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
